Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 02 s. 2023 January 10, 2023 DIR. RAMEL F. JAMEN Regional Director, DSWD Region-X DSWD Field Office X, Masterson Avenue Upper Carmen, Cagayan de Oro City Dear RD Jamen: This has reference to your letter dated 14 September 2022 requesting for this Department's opinion relative to Ordinance No. 1240-2022 enacted by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Ozamiz City on August 30, 2022, entitled: "AN ORDINANCE ENFORCING THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE AND REQUIRING NATIONAL GOVERNMENT AGENCIES TO SEEK PRIOR CONSULTATION AND APPROVAL FROM THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT OF OZAMIZ BEFORE THE CONDUCT OF NATIONAL ACTIVITIES, PROJECTS, OR PROGRAMS IN OZAMIZ CITY'. Per your letter, on September 6, 2022, your Office received a communication from the Office of the Administrator of the City of Ozamiz, stating, among others, that before the scheduled Social Pension 3rd Quarter Pay-Out can be conducted on September 13-16, compliance to the aforesaid ordinance must be made. It is your position that your Office's conduct of pay-out activities will inevitably redound to the benefit of the constituents of the concerned local government and that your Office is committed to its mandate to provide social protection programs to the poor, vulnerable and disadvantaged population. Hence, your herein request for legal opinion. May it be respectfully noted at the outset that the date of the Social Pension 3rd Quarter Pay-Out activity subject of your request has already lapsed. Be that as it may, since the Ordinance in question appears to be still pending review, we deem it proper to still render an opinion on the matter and recommend courses of action thereto. It appears that your request for legal opinions delves on the validity of Ordinance No. 1240-2022 of Ozamiz City. Validity refers to the substantive requirement of an ordinance, whether the same is consistent with the Constitution and laws. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

While we are cognizant of the intention of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Ozamiz City 'in this particular enactment, we observed that the third Whereas Clause of the subject ordinance, reads: 'Whereas, Section 27 of the same Code provides that no project or program shall be implemented by the govemment authorities unless the consultations mentioned in Section 2(c) are complied with, and prior approval of the sanggunian concemed is obtained. " It seems that the above-quoted was intended to require national government agencies to consult LGUs in the implementation of ALL its projects, programs or activities, so that appropriate approval of the sanggunian will be provided. In this regard, the case of Bangus Fry Fisherfolk Diwata Magbuhos vs. Lanzanasl, is instructive. In the said case, the Supreme Court had the opportunity to interpret Sections 26 and 27 of the LGC, which we quote: "Congress introduced Sections 26 and 27 in the Local Govemment Code to emphasize the legislative concem for the maintenance of a sound ecology and clean environment. These provisions require every national govemment agency or govemment-owned and controlled corporation to hold prior consultations with the local govemment unit concemed and to secure the prior approval of its sanggunian before implementing any project or program that may cause pollution, climatic change, depletion of non- renewable resources, loss of cropland, rangeland, or forest cover and extinction of animal or plant species. Sections 26 and 27 respectively provide: SECTION 26. Duty of National Govemment Agencies in the Maintenance of Ecological Balance. — It shall be the duty of every national agency or govemment-owned or -controlled corporation authorizing or involved in the planning and implementation of any project or program that may cause pollution, climatic change, depletion of non-renewable resources, loss of cropland, rangeland, or forest cover, and extinction of animal or plant species, to consult with the local govemment units, nongovemmental organizations, and other sectors concemed and explain the goals and objectives of the project or program, its impact upon the people and the community in terms of environmental or ecological balance, and the measures that will be undertaken to prevent or minimize the adverse effects thereof. SECTION 27. Prior Consultations Required. — No project or program shall be implemented by govemment authorities unless the consultations mentioned in Sections 2 (c) and 26 hereof are complied with, and prior approval of the sanggunian concemed is obtained: Provided, That occupants in areas where such projects are to be implemented shall notbe evicted unless appropriate relocation sites have been provided, in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution. 1 G.R. No. 131442, 10 July 2003 Page 2 of 4

In Lina, Jr. vs. Pafio, the Court interpreted these provisions in this manner: Section 27 of the Code should be read in conjunction with Section 26 thereof. Thus, the projects and programs mentioned in Section 27 should be interpreted to mean projects and programs whose effects are among those enumerated in Sections 26 and 27, to wit, those that: (1) may cause pollution; (2) may bring about climate change; (3) may cause the depletion of non-renewable resources; (4) may result in loss of crop land, rangeland, or forest cover; (5) may eradicate certain animal or plat species; and (6) other projects or programs that may call for the eviction of a particular group of people residing in the locality where these will be implemented. " From the foregoing, it is apparent that the projects and programs mentioned in Section 27 of the LGC that needs approval from the sanggunian are the following: 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. may cause pollution; may bring about climate change; may cause depletion of non-renewable resources; may result in loss of crop land, rangeland, or forest cover; may eradicated certain animal species; and other projects or programs that may call for the eviction of particular group of people residing in the locality where these will be implemented. This puts into issue the propriety of invoking Section 27 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) by the said sanggunian if the sole purpose is to require the approval of ALL projects, programs, and activities of national government agencies by the sangguniang panlungsod of the said LGU, where in fact, the Supreme Court has already settled as to what matters are covered or those that are statutorily required to seek the approval of the sanggunian. At this juncture, it may be well to note that per verification with Mr. Edgel G. Vedra, Local Government Operations Officer (CLGOO) of DILG-Ozamiz City, the said Ordinance was already forwarded by the Sangguniang Secretary to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Misamis Occidental pursuant to Section 56 of LGC. Under the said provision of the LGC, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan may declare such ordinance invalid or in part when such ordinance is beyond the power conferred upon the Sangguniang Panlungsod concerned. This was elucidated further by the Supreme Court in Moday vs. Court of Appeals (G.R. No. 107916, 20 February 1997), where the High Court ruled that the only ground upon which a provincial board may declare any municipal resolution or ordinance invalid is when such resolution or ordinance is beyond the powers conferred upon by the said council. Absolutely no other ground is recognized by the law (DILG Opinion No. 03, s. 1999). Thus, we shall forward your concern on the validity of the subject Ordinance as well as our initial finding thereto to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Misamis Occidental for its appropriate action. Page 3 of 4

However, as to its effectivity or such time when the ordinance is made effective and can already be implemented and given full force and effect, Section 59 of the LGC Provides that an ordinance of a local government unit becomes effective as of the date the framers of such ordinance would like it to be effective and in the absence•of such effectivity clause, the same shall take effect after ten (10) days from the date a copy thereof is posted in a bulletin board at the entrance of the city/municipal hall and in at least two (2) other conspicuous places in the local government unit concerned. Accordingly and as a matter course, the herein Ordinance of Ozamiz City shall already be given its legal effect and implemented even if the same is still pending review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. This opinion should be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent agencies and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY ATTY. ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: R R. LLAMAS ecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OU LLA/JVRULRALLD/rrao/clp copy furnish: DIR. WILHELM M.
